A vignette to demonstrate how to use PsyR to enact Post-Hoc Analysis of Variance via Confidence Intervals in a mixed (between x within) design, as in chapter 7 of @bird2004.

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

## The Packages

To use Psy to calculate confidence intervals over contrast effects, we will use a workflow that uses functions from [afex](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/afex/versions/1.4-1) to implement ANOVA models, and [emmeans](https://rvlenth.github.io/emmeans/) to obtain estimated marginal means and the required contrast estimates. So let's load those packages, and any others that are helpful for our workflow.

```{r setup}
library(PsyR)
library(tidyverse)
library(emmeans)
library(afex)
```

## The Data

Lets load the data, then call the `head()` function to print the first 5 rows.

```{r loaddata, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
data(social_anxiety)
head(social_anxiety, 5) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "html", table.attr = "style='width:50%;'")
```

Have you forgotten the details of the social anxiety dataframe? Call the help function using `?df` to open its documentation.

```{r, what_socialanx, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
?social_anxiety
```

Time for some tidying! Within the `mutate()` function, lets transform our existing columns. First, using `fct_relevel()`, the "Session" column is changed to the Factor datatype, and then organised according to chronological order. Next, the Group column is assigned as a factor, and then recoded such that treatment type is labelled with some more human readable names.

```{r longform}
social_anxiety <- social_anxiety %>%
  mutate(
    Session = fct_relevel(
      Session, "Pre", "Post", "FU1", "FU2"
    ),
    Group = factor(Group),
    Group = fct_recode(
      Group,
      "New" = "1",
      "Standard" = "2",
      "MinContact" = "3"
    )
  )
```

Time to visualise our data. Using `ggplot()`, lets take in our social anxiety dataframe. Next, lets call `aes()` and create a canvas with "Session" on the X axis, "Score" on the Y axis. Lets also colour-code our groups by calling fill: [New]{style="color: OrangeRed;"}, [Standard]{style="color: OliveDrab;"}, [MinContact]{style="color: Blue;"}.

```{r boxplotit, fig.width = 7.1, fig.height = 4}
social_anxiety %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Session, y = Score, fill = Group)) +
    geom_boxplot() +
    theme_classic(base_size = 14)
```

## The Analysis 

Lets prepare to run some statistical tests!

Here we will create the building blocks of our eventual ANOVA output. First, lets specify that we want a multivariate analysis, using the `afex_options()` function. Next, lets create a new object *mod*. To create *mod*, call the `aov_ez()` function which takes in the "Subject" column to identify subjects, the "Score" column as the dependent variable, the social_anxiety dataframe, the "Session" column set as within-subjects, and the "Group" column set as between-subjects. 

```{r model}
# set emmeans option to multivariate
afex_options(emmeans_model = "multivariate")

# perform the statistical model
mod <- aov_ez(
  "Subject", 
  "Score", 
  social_anxiety, 
  within = "Session",
  between = "Group"
)

emms_win <- emmeans(mod, "Session")
knitr::kable(emms_win, digits = 3)
```

Lets define and obtain our contrast tables. To do so, create the *win_contrasts* object, calling `list()` to define our contrasts, which compare the following:

- "Pre-Rest" - The difference between

- "Post-FUs" - The difference between

- "FU1-FU2" - The difference between

We can now generate our ANOVA table. To do so, create the *win_fx* object. Then, call the `contrast()` function from the emmeans package, setting *emms_win* in the "object" argument and our newly defined *win_contrasts* in the "method" argument.



```{r, win}
win_contrasts <- list(
  "Pre-Rest" = c(1, -1/3, -1/3, -1/3),
  "Post-FUs" = c(0, 1, -0.5, -0.5),
  "FU1-FU2" = c(0, 0, 1, -1)
) 

win_fx <- contrast(emms_win, win_contrasts)
knitr::kable(win_fx, digits = 3)
```

text

```{r, btwn}

btwn_contrasts <- list(
  "Ts-C" = c(0.5, 0.5, -1),
  "NT-ST" = c(1, -1, 0)
) 

emms_btwn <- emmeans(mod, "Group")

btwn_fx <- contrast(emms_btwn, btwn_contrasts)
knitr::kable(btwn_fx, digits = 3)
```

text

```{r, int}

emms_int <- emmeans(
  mod, c("Group", "Session")
)

int_fx <- contrast(
  emms_int,
  interaction = list(btwn_contrasts, win_contrasts)
)
int_fx
knitr::kable(int_fx, digits = 3)
```

A Priori Confidence

Here we replicate the bonferroni correction first presented in chapter 7

```{r, bon}

all_fx <- c(win_fx, btwn_fx, int_fx)
family_list = list("w", "b", "bw") 
alphas = .05 # 3 * alpha / nk

psyci(
  model = mod, contrast_tables = all_fx, method = "bf", 
  family_list = family_list, between_factors = list("Group"),
  within_factors = list("Session"), alpha = alphas
)

```

Next, we run the exact same but using the post-hoc method

```{r, psyci}

psyci(
  model = mod, contrast_tables = all_fx, method = "ph", 
  family_list = family_list, between_factors = list("Group"),
  within_factors = list("Session"), alpha = alphas
)

```
